newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee surges, but ends off contract highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee surges, but ends off contract highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures ended up sharply in volatile trading on Wednesday, but prices came reeling off highs after an official from Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said a 1996/97 crop estimate of 8.3 million bags released earlier was erroneous.
The Federation reiterated that its previous forecast of 10.4 million bags, made last week, still stands. A spokesman said today's lower forecast had been based on an erroneous calculation.

"The calculation was wrong," said Romn Medina, explaining that he failed to take into account 2 million bags of January to March production. He said production for the coffee year was still seen at a level of about 10.4 million bags, down from 12.9 million in the 1995/96 coffee year.

Most-active May coffee bounded to fresh life-of-contract of 177.00 cents per lb on the 8.3 million-bag Colombian forecast, before closing at 172.85 cents, up 9.60 cents on the day. May reached a low of 165.60 cents.
Spot March surged 11.30 cents, to 185.45 cents, a two-year high on the continuous weekly chart, but off its new contract high of 189.00 cents.

"When the 8.3 million estimate came out, everyone said buy and stops were touched off," one floor trader said. "When they said it was really 10.4 million everyone said sell. But nothing has changed. There is still no coffee."
Low levels of consumer and producer stocks are at the root of the steep run-up in the futures market, which has seen coffee prices rocket more than 50 percent since the beginning of the year.
Outlooks for lower harvests in many Latin American countries, including Colombia, have compounded supply concerns.
"The market is definately worried about tight supplies," said Refco Inc analyst Ann Prendergast. "And this (the erroneous Colombian estimate) is keeping that fear raw.

"Even if the Colombia estimate is false, the technical structure has been rearranged and (the market) looks poised to make further advances. However, people may be cautious about pushing it ahead without some other news," she added.

The nearby March/May switch, a barometer of near-term availability, ballooned to 12.60 cents, up from 10.90 cents at the close Tuesday. May/July widened to 8.60 cents from 6.90 cents the previous session.

After the close, the CSCE reported stocks certified for delivery against the exchange rose by 2,000 60-kg bags, to 26,045 bags -- the equivalent of about 100 lots. However, open interest in the March contract remained high at 3,508 lots.
"Two thousands bags does not make a difference," one trader said. "Maybe if it was up 20,000 bags it might have an effect on the market."
Refco's Prendergast said that while the market is likely to pull back in a technical correction, the bulltrend remained firmly intact.
"I do not see anything in the near term to make this market back off," she said. "I would not be surprised to see prices get up into the 190s."
Turnover on Wednesday reached an estimated 13,730 lots, up from Tuesday's official tally of 10,202 lots.
